questions.question: Report the five compartments recorded on the most reaction-like events. Give the compartment name, that number of events, and the share of all compartment records on reaction-like events it accounts for, as a percentage rounded to one decimal place. Use columns compartment, events and pct, ordered by highest count first, then alphabetically by compartment.

queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:compartment]->(c:Compartment)
WITH c, count(DISTINCT r) AS events
WITH collect({name: c.displayName, events: events}) AS rows, sum(events) AS total
UNWIND rows AS row
WITH row.name AS compartment, row.events AS events, total
ORDER BY events DESC, compartment
LIMIT 5
RETURN compartment, events, round(100.0 * events / total, 1) AS pct
queries.sql: WITH cnt AS (SELECT rc.compartment AS c, COUNT(DISTINCT rc.DB_ID) AS n FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_compartment rc JOIN Compartment cm ON cm.DB_ID = rc.compartment GROUP BY rc.compartment) SELECT d._displayName AS compartment, cnt.n AS events, ROUND(100.0 * cnt.n / SUM(cnt.n) OVER (), 1) AS pct FROM cnt JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = cnt.c ORDER BY events DESC, compartment LIMIT 5;

questions.question: Rank the compartments by how many Homo sapiens reaction-like events record them, highest count first, with equal counts sharing a rank. What rank does the compartment named "endoplasmic reticulum membrane" hold?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
MATCH (r)-[:compartment]->(c:Compartment)
WITH c, count(DISTINCT r) AS n
WITH collect({name: c.displayName, n: n}) AS rows
WITH rows, [x IN rows WHERE x.name = 'endoplasmic reticulum membrane'][0].n AS target
RETURN size([x IN rows WHERE x.n > target]) + 1
queries.sql: WITH cnt AS (SELECT rc.compartment AS c, COUNT(DISTINCT rc.DB_ID) AS n FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_compartment rc JOIN Compartment cm ON cm.DB_ID = rc.compartment JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = rc.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' GROUP BY rc.compartment), rk AS (SELECT c, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY n DESC) AS r FROM cnt) SELECT rk.r FROM rk JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = rk.c WHERE d._displayName = 'endoplasmic reticulum membrane';

questions.question: For each of the three species with the most reaction-like events, report how many distinct compartments those events record, how many distinct physical entities are an input to them, and how many distinct GO molecular functions their catalyst activities record. Use columns species, compartments, inputs and functions, ordered by species name.

queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(s:Species)
WITH s, count(DISTINCT r) AS total
ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 3
CALL { WITH s
  MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(s)
  MATCH (r)-[:compartment]->(c:Compartment)
  RETURN count(DISTINCT c) AS compartments }
CALL { WITH s
  MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(s)
  MATCH (r)-[:input]->(i)
  RETURN count(DISTINCT i) AS inputs }
CALL { WITH s
  MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(s)
  MATCH (r)-[:catalystActivity]->(:CatalystActivity)-[:activity]->(f:GO_MolecularFunction)
  RETURN count(DISTINCT f) AS functions }
RETURN s.displayName AS species, compartments, inputs, functions
ORDER BY species
queries.sql: WITH sp AS (SELECT es.species AS s, COUNT(DISTINCT es.DB_ID) AS total FROM Event_2_species es JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = es.DB_ID GROUP BY es.species ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 3) SELECT d._displayName AS species, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT rc.compartment) FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_compartment rc JOIN Compartment cm ON cm.DB_ID = rc.compartment JOIN Event_2_species e1 ON e1.DB_ID = rc.DB_ID WHERE e1.species = sp.s) AS compartments, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ri.input) FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_input ri JOIN Event_2_species e2 ON e2.DB_ID = ri.DB_ID WHERE e2.species = sp.s) AS inputs, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ca.activity) FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_catalystActivity rca JOIN CatalystActivity ca ON ca.DB_ID = rca.catalystActivity JOIN Event_2_species e3 ON e3.DB_ID = rca.DB_ID WHERE e3.species = sp.s) AS functions FROM sp JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = sp.s ORDER BY species;

questions.question: For each of the three species with the most reaction-like events, take that species' pathways that directly contain at least one reaction-like event. How many of them contain more than the mean number for their own species? Use columns species and pathways, ordered by species name.

queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(s:Species)
WITH s, count(DISTINCT r) AS total
ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 3
MATCH (p:Pathway)-[:species]->(s)
MATCH (p)-[:hasEvent]->(e:ReactionLikeEvent)
WITH s, p, count(DISTINCT e) AS n
WITH s, collect(n) AS ns
WITH s, ns, reduce(a = 0.0, x IN ns | a + x) / size(ns) AS mean
RETURN s.displayName AS species, size([x IN ns WHERE x > mean]) AS pathways
ORDER BY species
queries.sql: WITH sp AS (SELECT es.species AS s, COUNT(DISTINCT es.DB_ID) AS total FROM Event_2_species es JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = es.DB_ID GROUP BY es.species ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 3), cnt AS (SELECT ps.species AS s, he.DB_ID AS p, COUNT(DISTINCT he.hasEvent) AS n FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = he.hasEvent JOIN Event_2_species ps ON ps.DB_ID = he.DB_ID JOIN sp ON sp.s = ps.species GROUP BY ps.species, he.DB_ID), m AS (SELECT s, p, n, AVG(n) OVER (PARTITION BY s) AS mean FROM cnt) SELECT d._displayName AS species, COUNT(*) AS pathways FROM m JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = m.s WHERE m.n > m.mean GROUP BY m.s, d._displayName ORDER BY species;

questions.question: The pathway with stable identifier R-HSA-168256 directly contains three pathways. For each of those three, report the two pathways it directly contains that themselves directly contain the most reaction-like events, breaking ties alphabetically by name. Use columns parent, child and reactions, ordered by parent name, then by highest count first, then by child name.

expected.child: Immunoregulatory interactions between a Lymphoid and a non-Lymphoid cell
ROS and RNS production in phagocytes

queries.cypher:
MATCH (:Pathway {stId:'R-HSA-168256'})-[:hasEvent]->(parent:Pathway)-[:hasEvent]->(child:Pathway)
MATCH (child)-[:hasEvent]->(e:ReactionLikeEvent)
WITH parent, child, count(DISTINCT e) AS reactions
ORDER BY reactions DESC, child.displayName
WITH parent, collect({child: child.displayName, reactions: reactions})[0..2] AS top
UNWIND top AS t
RETURN parent.displayName AS parent, t.child AS child, t.reactions AS reactions
ORDER BY parent, reactions DESC, child
queries.sql: WITH cnt AS (SELECT r1.hasEvent AS parent, r2.hasEvent AS child, COUNT(DISTINCT r3.hasEvent) AS reactions FROM DatabaseObject o JOIN StableIdentifier si ON si.DB_ID = o.stableIdentifier AND si.identifier = 'R-HSA-168256' JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent r1 ON r1.DB_ID = o.DB_ID JOIN Pathway p1 ON p1.DB_ID = r1.hasEvent JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent r2 ON r2.DB_ID = r1.hasEvent JOIN Pathway p2 ON p2.DB_ID = r2.hasEvent JOIN Pathway_2_hasEvent r3 ON r3.DB_ID = r2.hasEvent JOIN ReactionlikeEvent rle ON rle.DB_ID = r3.hasEvent GROUP BY r1.hasEvent, r2.hasEvent), rk AS (SELECT c.parent, c.child, c.reactions, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.parent ORDER BY c.reactions DESC, dc._displayName) AS rn FROM cnt c JOIN DatabaseObject dc ON dc.DB_ID = c.child) SELECT dp._displayName AS parent, dc._displayName AS child, rk.reactions AS reactions FROM rk JOIN DatabaseObject dp ON dp.DB_ID = rk.parent JOIN DatabaseObject dc ON dc.DB_ID = rk.child WHERE rk.rn <= 2 ORDER BY parent, reactions DESC, child;

questions.question: Consider the Homo sapiens reaction-like events that take at least one input, grouped by how many distinct input entities they take. Report the five largest groups: the number of inputs, how many events are in the group, and the group's share of those events as a percentage rounded to one decimal place. Use columns inputs, events and pct, ordered by most events first, then by fewest inputs.

queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
MATCH (r)-[:input]->(i)
WITH r, count(DISTINCT i) AS inputs
WITH inputs, count(r) AS events
WITH collect({inputs: inputs, events: events}) AS rows, sum(events) AS total
UNWIND rows AS row
WITH row.inputs AS inputs, row.events AS events, total
ORDER BY events DESC, inputs
LIMIT 5
RETURN inputs, events, round(100.0 * events / total, 1) AS pct
queries.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT ri.DB_ID AS r, COUNT(DISTINCT ri.input) AS inputs FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_input ri JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = ri.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' GROUP BY ri.DB_ID), grp AS (SELECT inputs, COUNT(*) AS events FROM per GROUP BY inputs) SELECT inputs, events, ROUND(100.0 * events / SUM(events) OVER (), 1) AS pct FROM grp ORDER BY events DESC, inputs LIMIT 5;

questions.question: Among Homo sapiens pathways that directly contain at least twenty reaction-like events, which records the highest number of distinct input entities per directly contained reaction-like event? Give its name.

queries.cypher:
MATCH (p:Pathway)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
MATCH (p)-[:hasEvent]->(e:ReactionLikeEvent)
WITH p, count(DISTINCT e) AS events
WHERE events >= 20
MATCH (p)-[:hasEvent]->(:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:input]->(i)
WITH p, events, count(DISTINCT i) AS inputs
ORDER BY 1.0 * inputs / events DESC
LIMIT 1
RETURN p.displayName
queries.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT he.DB_ID AS p, COUNT(DISTINCT he.hasEvent) AS events FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN ReactionlikeEvent r ON r.DB_ID = he.hasEvent JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = he.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' GROUP BY he.DB_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT he.hasEvent) >= 20), inp AS (SELECT he.DB_ID AS p, COUNT(DISTINCT ri.input) AS inputs FROM Pathway_2_hasEvent he JOIN ReactionlikeEvent_2_input ri ON ri.DB_ID = he.hasEvent GROUP BY he.DB_ID) SELECT d._displayName FROM ev JOIN inp ON inp.p = ev.p JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = ev.p ORDER BY inp.inputs / ev.events DESC LIMIT 1;

questions.question: How many Homo sapiens pathways have been through any kind of curation act by an edit whose author is affiliated with an organisation whose name contains "University"?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (p:Pathway)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
MATCH (p)-[:created|modified|authored|reviewed|revised|internalReviewed|edited|structureModified]-(ie:InstanceEdit)
MATCH (ie)<-[:author]-(:Person)-[:affiliation]->(af:Affiliation)
WHERE any(x IN af.name WHERE x CONTAINS 'University')
RETURN count(DISTINCT p)
queries.sql: WITH hs AS (SELECT pw.DB_ID AS p FROM Pathway pw JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens'), cur AS (SELECT hs.p AS obj, d.created AS edit FROM hs JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = hs.p WHERE d.created IS NOT NULL UNION SELECT hs.p, m.modified FROM hs JOIN DatabaseObject_2_modified m ON m.DB_ID = hs.p UNION SELECT hs.p, a.authored FROM hs JOIN Event_2_authored a ON a.DB_ID = hs.p UNION SELECT hs.p, r.reviewed FROM hs JOIN Event_2_reviewed r ON r.DB_ID = hs.p UNION SELECT hs.p, v.revised FROM hs JOIN Event_2_revised v ON v.DB_ID = hs.p UNION SELECT hs.p, i.internalReviewed FROM hs JOIN Event_2_internalReviewed i ON i.DB_ID = hs.p UNION SELECT hs.p, e.edited FROM hs JOIN Event_2_edited e ON e.DB_ID = hs.p UNION SELECT hs.p, s.structureModified FROM hs JOIN Event_2_structureModified s ON s.DB_ID = hs.p) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cur.obj) FROM cur JOIN InstanceEdit_2_author ia ON ia.DB_ID = cur.edit JOIN Person_2_affiliation pa ON pa.DB_ID = ia.author JOIN Affiliation_2_name an ON an.DB_ID = pa.affiliation AND an.name LIKE '%University%';

questions.divergence: Reactome's relational and graph dumps of release 97 hold different InstanceEdit sets (126,230 rows against 160,392 nodes), and their edit->author links differ with them: 126,390 rows in InstanceEdit_2_author against 160,516 :author relationships, counted directly rather than through this question. Every endpoint of this question agrees across the stores - 184 affiliations whose name contains University, 250 people affiliated with one, 502 person-affiliation links, and 2,883 Homo sapiens pathways carrying a curation act whose edit has an author - so what differs is only which edit each pathway is linked to, and therefore whose affiliation is reached. TypeDB is loaded from the graph, so it matches Neo4j.

questions.question: Counting a component of a complex, a member or candidate of a set, and the repeated unit of a polymer all as parts, how many physical entities are directly a part of at least three different wholes?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (w:PhysicalEntity)-[:hasComponent|hasMember|hasCandidate|repeatedUnit]->(x:PhysicalEntity)
WITH x, count(DISTINCT w) AS n
WHERE n >= 3
RETURN count(x)
queries.sql: WITH parts AS (SELECT DB_ID AS whole, hasComponent AS part FROM Complex_2_hasComponent UNION SELECT DB_ID, hasMember FROM EntitySet_2_hasMember UNION SELECT DB_ID, hasCandidate FROM CandidateSet_2_hasCandidate UNION SELECT DB_ID, repeatedUnit FROM Polymer_2_repeatedUnit) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT part FROM parts GROUP BY part HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT whole) >= 3) t;

questions.divergence: Reactome's relational and graph dumps of release 97 disagree on Complex: the graph omits instances the relational dump has. Confirmed for this question by diffing the answer sets — the single extra entity SQL reports is 5663163 (Per1 gene [nucleoplasm]), whose three containing complexes in MySQL are 8878911, 9926587 and 9933412; the first two have no node in Neo4j at all, so its whole-count falls from 3 to 1 there. TypeDB is loaded from the graph, so it matches Neo4j.

questions.question: Counting inputs, outputs and required input components all as ways of taking part, how many physical entities take part in more than 100 distinct Homo sapiens reaction-like events?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
MATCH (r)-[:input|output|requiredInputComponent]->(x:PhysicalEntity)
WITH x, count(DISTINCT r) AS n
WHERE n > 100
RETURN count(x)
queries.sql: WITH part AS (SELECT DB_ID AS ev, input AS pe FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_input UNION SELECT DB_ID, output FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_output UNION SELECT DB_ID, requiredInputComponent FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_requiredInputComponent), hs AS (SELECT DISTINCT es.DB_ID AS ev FROM Event_2_species es JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens') SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT p.pe FROM part p JOIN hs ON hs.ev = p.ev GROUP BY p.pe HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.ev) > 100) t;

questions.question: Reactome can record that one event explicitly does not precede another, together with the reason for the exclusion. How many distinct pairs of events have such an exclusion recorded with no reason?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (b:Event)-[:negativePrecedingEvent]->(npe:NegativePrecedingEvent)-[:precedingEvent]->(a:Event)
WHERE NOT EXISTS { (npe)-[:reason]->() }
WITH DISTINCT a, b
RETURN count(*)
queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ne.DB_ID AS following, pe.precedingEvent AS excluded FROM Event_2_negativePrecedingEvent ne JOIN NegativePrecedingEvent np ON np.DB_ID = ne.negativePrecedingEvent AND np.reason IS NULL JOIN NegativePrecedingEvent_2_precedingEvent pe ON pe.DB_ID = np.DB_ID) t;

questions.question: Among Homo sapiens reaction-like events, a disease entity may be recorded as standing in for the normal entity it replaces. How many distinct pairs of a disease entity and its normal entity are both Complexes that have no part in common — no component, member, candidate or repeated unit shared between them?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
MATCH (r)-[:entityFunctionalStatus]->(efs:EntityFunctionalStatus)
MATCH (efs)-[:diseaseEntity]->(de:Complex)
MATCH (efs)-[:normalEntity]->(ne:Complex)
WHERE NOT EXISTS {
  MATCH (de)-[:hasComponent|hasMember|hasCandidate|repeatedUnit]->(x)
  MATCH (ne)-[:hasComponent|hasMember|hasCandidate|repeatedUnit]->(x) }
WITH DISTINCT de, ne
RETURN count(*)
queries.sql: WITH parts AS (SELECT DB_ID AS whole, hasComponent AS part FROM Complex_2_hasComponent UNION SELECT DB_ID, hasMember FROM EntitySet_2_hasMember UNION SELECT DB_ID, hasCandidate FROM CandidateSet_2_hasCandidate UNION SELECT DB_ID, repeatedUnit FROM Polymer_2_repeatedUnit) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT efs.diseaseEntity AS de, efs.normalEntity AS ne FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_entityFunctionalStatus re JOIN EntityFunctionalStatus efs ON efs.DB_ID = re.entityFunctionalStatus JOIN Complex dc ON dc.DB_ID = efs.diseaseEntity JOIN Complex nc ON nc.DB_ID = efs.normalEntity JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = re.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens' WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM parts p1 JOIN parts p2 ON p2.part = p1.part WHERE p1.whole = efs.diseaseEntity AND p2.whole = efs.normalEntity)) t;

questions.question: Physical entity has several direct subtypes in the Reactome class hierarchy. For how many of them is at least one instance an input to a Homo sapiens reaction-like event?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (r:ReactionLikeEvent)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
MATCH (r)-[:input]->(x)
UNWIND ['EntitySet','Cell','Drug','Complex','GenomeEncodedEntity','OtherEntity','Polymer','SimpleEntity'] AS t
WITH x, t WHERE t IN labels(x)
RETURN count(DISTINCT t)
queries.sql: WITH hsinput AS (SELECT DISTINCT ri.input AS pe FROM ReactionlikeEvent_2_input ri JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = ri.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens') SELECT (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hsinput JOIN EntitySet t ON t.DB_ID = hsinput.pe)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hsinput JOIN Cell t ON t.DB_ID = hsinput.pe)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hsinput JOIN Drug t ON t.DB_ID = hsinput.pe)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hsinput JOIN Complex t ON t.DB_ID = hsinput.pe)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hsinput JOIN GenomeEncodedEntity t ON t.DB_ID = hsinput.pe)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hsinput JOIN OtherEntity t ON t.DB_ID = hsinput.pe)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hsinput JOIN Polymer t ON t.DB_ID = hsinput.pe)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hsinput JOIN SimpleEntity t ON t.DB_ID = hsinput.pe)) AS subtypes;

questions.question: An object may be created, modified, authored, reviewed, internally reviewed, revised, edited or structurally modified by an edit — the kinds of curation act. How many Homo sapiens pathways have been through at least five different kinds?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (p:Pathway)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
WITH p,
  (CASE WHEN EXISTS { (p)<-[:created]-(:InstanceEdit) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
   CASE WHEN EXISTS { (p)<-[:modified]-(:InstanceEdit) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
   CASE WHEN EXISTS { (p)<-[:authored]-(:InstanceEdit) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
   CASE WHEN EXISTS { (p)<-[:reviewed]-(:InstanceEdit) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
   CASE WHEN EXISTS { (p)<-[:revised]-(:InstanceEdit) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
   CASE WHEN EXISTS { (p)-[:internalReviewed]->(:InstanceEdit) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
   CASE WHEN EXISTS { (p)<-[:edited]-(:InstanceEdit) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
   CASE WHEN EXISTS { (p)-[:structureModified]->(:InstanceEdit) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS kinds
WHERE kinds >= 5
RETURN count(DISTINCT p)
queries.sql: WITH hs AS (SELECT DISTINCT pw.DB_ID AS p FROM Pathway pw JOIN Event_2_species es ON es.DB_ID = pw.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject sp ON sp.DB_ID = es.species AND sp._displayName = 'Homo sapiens') SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hs WHERE ((EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM DatabaseObject d WHERE d.DB_ID = hs.p AND d.created IS NOT NULL)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM DatabaseObject_2_modified m WHERE m.DB_ID = hs.p)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Event_2_authored a WHERE a.DB_ID = hs.p)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Event_2_reviewed r WHERE r.DB_ID = hs.p)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Event_2_revised v WHERE v.DB_ID = hs.p)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Event_2_internalReviewed i WHERE i.DB_ID = hs.p)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Event_2_edited e WHERE e.DB_ID = hs.p)) + (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Event_2_structureModified s WHERE s.DB_ID = hs.p))) >= 5;

questions.question: Reactome records several kinds of name: an object's display name, the names in its name slot, gene names, systematic names, a person's first name and surname, and an affiliation's names. Ignoring case, how many database objects go by a name of some kind that contains "PIK3" although their display name does not?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (x)
WHERE NOT toLower(coalesce(x.displayName, '')) CONTAINS 'pik3'
  AND (any(v IN coalesce(x.name, []) WHERE toLower(v) CONTAINS 'pik3')
    OR any(v IN coalesce(x.geneName, []) WHERE toLower(v) CONTAINS 'pik3')
    OR toLower(coalesce(x.systematicName, '')) CONTAINS 'pik3'
    OR toLower(coalesce(x.firstname, '')) CONTAINS 'pik3'
    OR toLower(coalesce(x.surname, '')) CONTAINS 'pik3')
RETURN count(x)
queries.sql: WITH names AS (SELECT DB_ID, name AS n FROM Event_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM PhysicalEntity_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM ReferenceEntity_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM ExternalOntology_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM GO_BiologicalProcess_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM GO_CellularComponent_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM GO_MolecularFunction_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM ControlledVocabulary_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM Taxon_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM FunctionalStatusType_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM ReferenceDatabase_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, name FROM Affiliation_2_name UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, geneName FROM ReferenceSequence_2_geneName UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, systematicName FROM PhysicalEntity WHERE systematicName IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, systematicName FROM ReactionlikeEvent WHERE systematicName IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, firstname FROM Person WHERE firstname IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, surname FROM Person WHERE surname IS NOT NULL) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT names.DB_ID) FROM names JOIN DatabaseObject d ON d.DB_ID = names.DB_ID WHERE names.n LIKE '%PIK3%' AND (d._displayName IS NULL OR d._displayName NOT LIKE '%PIK3%');

questions.divergence: The graph carries ReferenceDNASequence and ReferenceRNASequence nodes the relational dump does not have (624,054 ReferenceDNASequence nodes against 119,723 rows). Confirmed for this question by diffing the answer sets: the twelve extra objects Neo4j reports (db-ids 11395662 to 12781774, all reference DNA or RNA sequences for the gene HCST) each carry PIK3AP among their gene names and have no row in MySQL. TypeDB is loaded from the graph, so it matches Neo4j.

questions.question: Counting the names recorded in an entity's name slot rather than its display name, how many distinct names are carried both by a physical entity assigned to Homo sapiens and by a physical entity assigned to Bos taurus?

queries.cypher:
CALL {
  MATCH (p:PhysicalEntity)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
  UNWIND p.name AS n RETURN DISTINCT n, 'hs' AS k
  UNION
  MATCH (p:PhysicalEntity)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Bos taurus'})
  UNWIND p.name AS n RETURN DISTINCT n, 'bt' AS k
}
WITH n, count(*) AS c WHERE c = 2
RETURN count(n)
queries.sql: WITH pesp AS (SELECT DB_ID, species FROM GenomeEncodedEntity WHERE species IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM SimpleEntity WHERE species IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM Cell_2_species UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM Complex_2_species UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM EntitySet_2_species UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM Polymer_2_species), hs AS (SELECT DISTINCT n.name FROM PhysicalEntity_2_name n JOIN pesp ON pesp.DB_ID = n.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject s ON s.DB_ID = pesp.species AND s._displayName = 'Homo sapiens'), bt AS (SELECT DISTINCT n.name FROM PhysicalEntity_2_name n JOIN pesp ON pesp.DB_ID = n.DB_ID JOIN DatabaseObject s ON s.DB_ID = pesp.species AND s._displayName = 'Bos taurus') SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hs JOIN bt ON hs.name = bt.name;

questions.question: How many Homo sapiens physical entities share a non-empty name, taken from the name slot and matched exactly and case-sensitively, with a reference entity other than their own reference entity? An entity with no reference entity counts if it shares a name with any reference entity.

queries.cypher:
CALL {
  MATCH (p:PhysicalEntity)-[:species]->(:Species {displayName:'Homo sapiens'})
  UNWIND p.name AS n RETURN n, p AS x, 'pe' AS k
  UNION ALL
  MATCH (r:ReferenceEntity) UNWIND r.name AS n RETURN n, r AS x, 're' AS k
}
WITH n, collect(CASE WHEN k = 'pe' THEN x END) AS ps, collect(CASE WHEN k = 're' THEN x END) AS rs
WHERE n <> '' AND size(ps) > 0 AND size(rs) > 0
UNWIND ps AS p UNWIND rs AS r
WITH DISTINCT p, r WHERE NOT (p)-[:referenceEntity]->(r)
RETURN count(DISTINCT p)
queries.sql: WITH pesp AS (SELECT DB_ID, species FROM GenomeEncodedEntity WHERE species IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM SimpleEntity WHERE species IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM Cell_2_species UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM Complex_2_species UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM EntitySet_2_species UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, species FROM Polymer_2_species), hs AS (SELECT DISTINCT pesp.DB_ID FROM pesp JOIN DatabaseObject s ON s.DB_ID = pesp.species AND s._displayName = 'Homo sapiens'), refs AS (SELECT DB_ID, referenceEntity FROM EntityWithAccessionedSequence WHERE referenceEntity IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, referenceEntity FROM SimpleEntity WHERE referenceEntity IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT DB_ID, referenceEntity FROM Drug WHERE referenceEntity IS NOT NULL) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hs.DB_ID) FROM hs JOIN PhysicalEntity_2_name pn ON pn.DB_ID = hs.DB_ID JOIN ReferenceEntity_2_name rn ON BINARY rn.name = BINARY pn.name WHERE pn.name <> '' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM refs WHERE refs.DB_ID = hs.DB_ID AND refs.referenceEntity = rn.DB_ID);

questions.divergence: The relational dump holds a ReferenceGeneProduct the graph does not: 9663770 (UniProt:Q9JKQ2 SLC26A5), whose name SLC26A5 is also a name of the human entity 5216108 (SLC26A5 [plasma membrane]), which points at a different reference gene product (62142). Confirmed by diffing the answer sets: that entity is the single one MySQL reports and Neo4j does not. TypeDB is loaded from the graph, so it matches Neo4j. The question says non-empty because 65 Reactome name lists carry a trailing empty string (e.g. RHOG's ["RHOG", "RhoG", ""]); the TypeDB export drops it as a data-entry artefact, so without the exclusion Neo4j and MySQL match 22 more entities to reference entities through the empty string (2111 and 2112) while TypeDB reports 2089. MySQL's default collation compares strings case-insensitively; joining the two name tables without BINARY returns 5217, because human names such as INS then match names such as Ins on reference entities of other species.

questions.question: Reactome records seven kinds of name: display names, names in the name slot, gene names, systematic names, people's first names, surnames and affiliation names. Ignoring case, how many of these seven kinds have at least one value containing "ras"?

queries.cypher:
MATCH (x)
WITH max(CASE WHEN toLower(coalesce(x.displayName, '')) CONTAINS 'ras' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS display,
     max(CASE WHEN NOT x:Affiliation AND any(v IN coalesce(x.name, []) WHERE toLower(v) CONTAINS 'ras') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS curated,
     max(CASE WHEN x:Affiliation AND any(v IN coalesce(x.name, []) WHERE toLower(v) CONTAINS 'ras') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS affiliation,
     max(CASE WHEN any(v IN coalesce(x.geneName, []) WHERE toLower(v) CONTAINS 'ras') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS gene,
     max(CASE WHEN toLower(coalesce(x.systematicName, '')) CONTAINS 'ras' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS systematic,
     max(CASE WHEN toLower(coalesce(x.firstname, '')) CONTAINS 'ras' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS first,
     max(CASE WHEN toLower(coalesce(x.surname, '')) CONTAINS 'ras' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS surname
RETURN display + curated + affiliation + gene + systematic + first + surname AS kinds
